p.t: What does Jesun Ahmad Ushno do?
p.x: He builds production AI systems: machine learning products, retrieval-augmented generation and multi-agent fleets that run like a company, with roles, seats and jobs. He also runs three ventures: Immitly as Founder, and Brimwood Innovation and Climeam as Co-Founder.

Immitly, an immigration guidance platform, which he founded. Brimwood Innovation, a Toronto innovation hub he co-founded with Adam Sayani. Climeam, an AI-native creative studio he co-founded and whose work he directs.

Two machine learning papers in AIP Conference Proceedings (2023): one on fabric defect detection with the wavelet transform and a neural network (DOI 10.1063/5.0148618), one on an elitist particle swarm optimizer with mutation and adaptive inertia (DOI 10.1063/5.0148658). In 2026 he published four sole-author preprints on Zenodo: Peeking, Pooling, and a Locked Split (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24282470), Creditworthy Rejects (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24283751), Filtered Vector Search Is a Regime Map, Not a Leaderboard (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24283784), and Where MapReduce Catches Up (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24283816). He also wrote a book on data analytics (2025) and essays on Medium.

Zero-trust analytics. Excel, CSV and XML are processed in your browser. No bytes leave the machine. A web analytics platform for sensitive information. Files are parsed and analysed in the browser with Pyodide and WebAssembly, so the data never reaches a server. AI-driven insights run on the same principle: the machine you own does the work. Stack: Pyodide, React, TypeScript, WASM.

An autonomous predictive terminal for sports markets. An agent swarm that watches, models and acts on its own schedule. BigFish is a fleet, not a script. Agents watch the market, model outcomes and act on a schedule with no human in the loop. It is the clearest public example of how Jesun builds: roles, seats and jobs, run like a company. Stack: Python, ML, Automation.

Measures how a person draws. 32 metrics per session from coordinates, time and pressure. A research build, not a clinical product. Built during the mentAImage internship (Jan to Mar 2026). Seven drawing tasks, from clock drawing to two-hand loops. The pipeline reads tremor, pauses, speed and pressure stability, and maps 10 indicators to stress, anxiety, burnout and cognitive load scores. 35 sessions analysed. The validation study is the open work. Stack: Python, Signal processing, Feature extraction.

Private media converter. Video, audio and image conversion with FFmpeg.wasm. Zero uploads, zero tracking. A serverless media conversion platform. FFmpeg compiled to WebAssembly runs in the browser tab, so files are converted without ever being uploaded. Stack: FFmpeg.wasm, React, PWA.

Full-stack audio cleanup. Deep learning removes background noise and restores vocal clarity. A full-stack web application that cleans and enhances spoken audio. A PyTorch model removes background noise; FastAPI serves it. Stack: PyTorch, Audio DSP, FastAPI.

Peer-to-peer file sharing between iPhone and Windows. Scan a QR code, connect, share. No install. WebRTC moves files directly between devices in the browser. A QR code pairs them. Nothing sits on a server in between. Stack: WebRTC, PWA.

Privacy-focused asset generator for Chrome Web Store listings. Runs entirely in the browser. Store listing assets made in the browser tab, with nothing uploaded. Pinned on his GitHub profile. Stack: JavaScript, Canvas.

Wavelet transform plus neural network to detect and classify fabric defects. AIP Conference Proceedings. Published research: an autonomous framework that uses the wavelet transform to expose texture defects and a neural network to classify them. Try a live version of the wavelet step in the Lab. Stack: Wavelets, Neural networks, Computer vision.

Elitist particle swarm optimization with a mutation operator and adaptive inertia weight. AIP Conference Proceedings. Published research on global optimization: particle swarm optimization that keeps an elite, mutates to escape local minima and adapts inertia over time. A live version runs in the Lab. Stack: Optimization, Swarm intelligence.

p.x: He runs 58 public studies under one written standard, Standard v2, adopted 2026-11-08. Each states its question first and is graded on a verdict ladder: Draft, Proposed, Functional, Evaluated, v1.0 Released. Counts: 5 Draft, 1 Proposed, 39 Functional, 3 Evaluated, 1 v1.0 Released. His research spine asks how far an automated judge can be trusted.

On two GPU nodes joined by commodity 1 GbE, when does data-parallel training beat one node, and can a two-parameter link model measured in two minutes predict the answer before the training runs? Headline: On two NVIDIA GB10 nodes over 1 GbE, two nodes are slower than one in 9 of 12 cells, down to 0.069x (95% bootstrap interval 0.067 to 0.075) for the 92M-parameter model at accumulation 1, and a link model fitted before any two-node run predicted every cell's step time within 2.7%.

In randomized Upworthy headline tests, does phrasing a headline as a question change click-through rate, compared with non-question headlines shown in the same test? Headline: In the locked split of 465 eligible randomized tests, question headlines were associated with lower click-through than non-question headlines in the same tests: pooled odds ratio 0.8645 (95% CI 0.8335 to 0.8966), Upworthy 2013 to 2015 only.

On one consumer GPU, how much faster, lighter on memory, and how different in accuracy is a hand-written PyTorch training loop against a PyTorch Lightning baseline, and what do AMP, torch.compile, gradient checkpointing, profiling and data loading each... Headline: One of seven pre-registered hypotheses held: ResNet-18 training on EuroSAT was bound by data loading, not GPU compute, so AMP reached 1.13x throughput (95% CI 1.12 to 1.13) against its 1.30x prior and torch.compile 1.03x (95% CI 1.02 to 1.04) against 1.10x, on one RTX 5050 Laptop GPU with n = 2 seeds per arm.

Headline: On the 8 designed malformed records, the repair loop healed 3 (repair rate 0.375, Wilson 95% 0.137 to 0.694), and 2 of those 3 were flagged clamps that changed a stated value (silent failure rate 0.667, 95% 0.208 to 0.939); no language-model output was measured.

Do the LoRA, GRPO and DPO update rules behave as their derivations predict, against baselines and across seeds, on synthetic tasks small enough to check by hand? Headline: On a synthetic NumPy classification task, a rank 2 LoRA adapter (40 trainable weights) reaches mean held-out test accuracy 0.9039 (bootstrap 95% CI 0.8742 to 0.9305, 10 seeds), below full fine-tuning of all 64 weights at 0.9391 (CI 0.9219 to 0.9555). No real language model was trained.
